basics.name: Andrés Gómez Ramírez
basics.summary: Cybersecurity engineer, security researcher, and senior DevOps/cloud infrastructure engineer with 15+ years of experience across penetration testing, vulnerability research, intrusion detection, applied AI for security monitoring, and large-scale cloud & HPC infrastructure. PhD in Cybersecurity (Goethe University Frankfurt, in collaboration with CERN). Co-Founder & CEO of Sakundi.

work.summary: Teach within the Cybersecurity Master's program, covering blockchain security fundamentals.

Analyzed and developed cryptographic code and smart contracts for Panther, a privacy-enhancing protocol, with a focus on security review. Managed deployment pipelines and infrastructure for the protocol on the Polygon ecosystem.

Founded and lead a security, privacy, and digital identity startup, setting technical direction and client strategy. Deliver security audits, monitoring solutions, and identity infrastructure to enterprise and protocol clients. Designed and maintained reproducible, auditable deployment pipelines and infrastructure-as-code for client environments.

Designed, deployed, and maintained Linux-based on-premise and cloud infrastructure on AWS (EC2, EKS, S3, IAM, VPC) for blockchain-focused products. Provisioned and managed Kubernetes clusters and containerized microservices. Authored Terraform modules for infrastructure-as-code. Built CI/CD pipelines with GitHub Actions. Implemented observability with Grafana and Prometheus. Delivered infrastructure for blockchain ecosystems including EOSIO/Antelope, Ethereum, and Bitcoin networks.

Built and maintained the security monitoring and infrastructure management system for the ALICE High-Level Trigger (HLT) computing cluster using Zabbix. Managed infrastructure-as-code and configuration management using Puppet and Ansible, enforcing hardened baselines across hundreds of compute nodes. Worked with Vagrant and OpenStack for virtual environment provisioning; contributed to the HLT read-out upgrade for LHC Run 2 (published in JINST).

Researched deep learning (generative models) and isolation-based methods for intrusion detection and prevention on the Worldwide LHC Computing Grid (WLCG). Built a Python/Perl framework implementing the research; co-authored 3 peer-reviewed papers from this work.

Performed infrastructure assessments, penetration tests, source code audits, and vulnerability assessments for banks, software development companies, and ISPs. Identified and reported multiple CVEs, including a Microsoft DirectShow memory-overwrite vulnerability (MS13-056).
